title: How to transform LLM output into an RPG tiled room?
author: HalfTryhardSqr
selftext:
I am working on a text based RPG powered by a multi-agent AI enforcing a custom version of the Fate system.

Each agent is configured to work best in a specific task: there is a Creative-Agent which specializes in the narrative aspect of the game, there is an Observer-Agent that updates the data model of the game via function calls and enforces the system rules, and there is a GM-Agent that talks to the other agents, manages the game and takes care of player communications.

Currently the rooms and environment are an abstract json object without tiles, just a description, different objectives, NPCs, theme, optional challenges, etc... And it seems to work quite well for basic storylines and compliant players. Now I'd like to add another agent to the system: a Room-Agent which takes the narrative description of the room, generates a fully playable board/dungeon. The question is... How do you approach something like that?

I've got it to generate very basic layouts (for example, a camp with a few tents with chests and enemies guarding the entrances), but struggles with more requiring rooms such as a house with an organized layout and more content diversity and detail.

What are your thoughts? Do you have any idea on how to approach this Room-Agent?

comments.author: AdvAndInt
comments.body:
So to make sure I'm understanding what you're trying to accomplish. You want to take a structured JSON data set of a text descriptions of a given scene or level and you want an LLM to digest it and return a 2d grid that represents a top down view of the zone, something like a DND battlemap? 

Also, you should definitely join the discord in the sticky thread. We have an AI RPG channel that has had a lot of really good discussions related to what you're building. Come join us!

comments.author: No_Industry9653
comments.body: Maybe put together a dataset of descriptions -> room layouts and do custom training on it.
